newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Investors to get 30 pct of Kazakh Mangistau oil co.
newsitem.headline: Investors to get 30 pct of Kazakh Mangistau oil co.

text.p: Kazakhstan, which sold a 60 percent stake in its largest oil producer Mangistaumunaigaz to Indonesia's Central Asia Petroleum Ltd on Sunday, plans to sell another 30 percent to portfolio investors later this year.

"The remaining 40 percent are being divided between the workers of Mangistaumunaigaz who will get 10 percent and the state which will get 30 percent... It is planned to offer the state stake to investors on the stock market which we are now creating," Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Pavlov told a news conference on Monday.

The government of the former Soviet republic is planning to set in motion a viable shares market by the year-end. It will offer its stakes in around 60 large companies from Kazakhstan's potentially multi-billion oil and gas, metals and processing industries to portfolio investors.

The former Soviet republic, rich in natural resources and desperately in need of large direct investment to speed up its market reforms, hopes that many of these companies will become real "blue chips" and the core of the future shares market.

But Pavlov said that before being offered to portfolio investors, large local companies like Mangistaumunaigaz would have to convert their accounts to international standards and undergo auditing by a leading western auditor.
On Sunday the Kazakh government sold a 60 percent stake in Mangistaumunaigaz to Indonesia's Central Asia Petroleum Ltd for a total of $4.348 billion.

Pavlov, who chairs Kazakhstan's tender committee, said the Indonesian partner had pledged to invest $4.1 billion within 20 years, including $2 billion within the next five years. It is also paying a bonus to the government of $248 million.
